item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q005_cupredoxin_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe places these proteins together only at the fold level in the all-beta cupredoxin-like fold, not in one close functional family. Plastocyanin- and azurin-like blue copper proteins belong to the cupredoxin superfamily within that fold, where the conserved copper-site geometry supports electron-transfer annotation for appropriate homologs. Ephrin ectodomains and the N-terminal domain of peptidylarginine deiminase 4 are separate cupredoxin-like superfamilies/families: they share the beta-sandwich/Greek-key structural architecture but are not close cupredoxin homologs. Therefore copper binding, blue-copper redox chemistry, or electron-transfer function should not be transferred from plastocyanin/azurin to ephrins or to PAD4 merely because SCOPe assigns all three to the same fold; at most, the shared fold can justify remote structural templating of the core beta-sandwich, with functional residues and metal-binding sites checked independently.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
